title: Autotune harness for kernel choice and sparse-attention benchmark suite
creator: Nadia Chen
title_summary: Create an automated benchmarking harness that autotunes kernel selection and sparse-attention params and produces deterministic golden baselines with CI perf gates
description:
Background: Kernel selection and attention pathing are primary levers for latency and cost in Redwood's serving runtime. Current benchmarking is manual: engineers run ad-hoc mixes, tune heuristics, and occasionally update golden baselines. This leads to gaps between CI gates and production behavior (esp. for sparse/dilated attention variants and long-prefill paths).

Goal: Build an autotuning benchmark harness that: 1) runs mixed workloads (synthetic + sampled traces) across candidate kernel/attention configs, 2) produces deterministic golden baseline artifacts (seeded inputs, golden token-level latency histograms), 3) integrates with CI to gate regressions and surface configuration recommendations for the runtime selector. The harness should support parallel job orchestration, dataset slicing (short/long-prefill cohorts), and automated diff reports that highlight regressions at p50/p95/p99 and memory/throughput trade-offs.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run a configurable mixbench (user-defined weights) combining synthetic templates and sampled prod traces
Autotune job explores parameter grid (kernel choices, sparsity flags, queue length thresholds) and records deterministic per-token metrics
Golden artifacts (seeded workloads + summary histograms) are stored in S3 with stable keys and linked from the CI run
CI perf gate compares new runs vs golden baseline and fails when p95 latency increases > 8% or memory increases > 10% for high-impact cohorts
Generated diff report includes recommended kernel fallback (e.g., switch to fallback-kernel-v2 for long-prefill heavy mixes) and confidence score
implementation_notes: Runner built on top of the mixbench infra (reuse orchestration layer from ENG-21678), but add a deterministic seeding layer to ensure stable per-token traces
Parameter space initially limited to three kernel families + two sparse-attention flags to bound runtime (expandable via experiment configs)
Use prefix/KV cache warmup step to model prefill+decode paths accurately; measure decode-only vs prefill+decode separately
Store raw perf traces and token-level latencies to enable later root-cause analysis in Grafana/BigQuery
Autoscaler interaction: mark certain runs as "stress" that exercise autoscaler to observe realistic tail latency; run those at lower frequency to save cost
test_plan: Stage 1 (prototype): 30 synthetic runs across kernel grid, verify deterministic outputs repeat across 3 repeated runs
Stage 2 (trace mix): Add 50 sampled traces representing long-prefill sessions and verify p95 alignment with production telemetry within 10%
Stage 3 (CI integration): Add perf-gate job that runs nightly against golden and fails CI on regressions. Validate false-positive rate by running known-good commits for 2 weeks
Stage 4 (autotune): Implement simple greedy search that picks best kernel per cohort; compare against current heuristic and quantify cost savings/latency improvement
metrics_and_thresholds: p50 latency (ms) - track per-cohort; flag changes > 12%
p95 latency (ms) - primary CI metric; fail if > 8% regression on high-impact cohorts
GPU memory (MiB) - alert/fail thresholds set per-device class; fail if steady-state memory increases > 10%
throughput (tokens/s) - record to detect cost regressions (goal: no > 10% throughput drop at equal batch sizes)
runbook_and_operational_notes: How to add new kernel families: add an entry to autotune YAML with kernel id, compatible model families, estimated cost factor
When CI gate fails: triage steps include (1) reproduce locally with same seed, (2) run profiling to get kernel heatmap, (3) open ENG perf investigation ticket linking run artifacts
Cost controls: heavy grid searches should be gated behind 'expensive' flag and scheduled on dedicated bench pools to avoid affecting prod capacity
Retention: golden artifacts kept for 180 days; summary metrics persisted for 1 year for trend analysis
updates: 2025-02-12: Kickoff sync with runtime and bench teams. Agreed scope: limit initial parameter grid to 3 kernel families + 2 sparse flags.
2025-02-18: Prototype runner implemented (branch: feat/autotune-harness). Deterministic seeding added; first synthetic runs produced stable histograms.
2025-02-24: Integrated KV-warmup step; discovered decode-only vs prefill+decode deltas cause p95 shifts when prefix length > 1024 tokens. Added cohort slicing for long-prefill.
2025-02-28: Opened PR #5847 against mixbench orchestrator (github.com/redwood-inference/mixbench/pull/5847). Initial reviewer comments: need clearer artifact naming convention and S3 lifecycle tags.

2025-03-03: CI perf gate prototype job wired into nightly pipeline. Ran 12 candidate jobs; one kernel variant caused p95 regression of 11% on long-prefill cohort; marked as rejected by autotune. Preparing RCA.
2025-03-05: Addressed PR feedback, added stable artifact key format and lifecycle policy. Requesting runtime review and sign-off before merging to main.
comments: Priya Kapoor (PM) 2025-02-13: Please ensure golden cohorts align to customer-facing SLAs; we should include a "payment-batch" cohort from enterprise customers.
Ethan Brooks (SRE) 2025-02-25: When running stress variants that exercise autoscaler, tag runs with 'stress' to prevent accidental use for SLA comparisons.
Runtime lead (Ava Mitchell) 2025-03-01: Consider adding a secondary metric 'token stall time' to better capture prefill-induced stalls on condensed kernels.
Marco Alvarez (owner) 2025-03-04: Noted false-positive caused by noisy device telemetry on 2025-02-27 - added device health filter to harness.
next_steps: Finish runtime review and incorporate kernel-fallback suggestion logic into the selector (planned by 2025-03-12)
Merge PR and run a 2-week Canary where autotune recommendations are applied in a shadow mode to Dedicated pools
Iterate on CI gate thresholds after 2 weeks of data to minimize false positives while catching real regressions
Add an "experiment" mode to allow broader parameter sweeps for research with cost caps
